competitors.name: California Pizza Kitchen
competitors.action: CPK said it is expanding retail beyond frozen pizza for the first time since 1999, adding grocery-bound appetizers and entrées in the U.S. while also widening frozen-pizza distribution through Nestlé across Latin America, the Caribbean, Taiwan, Japan, and Shanghai.

competitors.name: Katie’s Pizza & Pasta / Katie’s CPG
competitors.action: Katie’s said its frozen pizzas drove 8.4% of frozen-pizza category growth in the natural channel and that new distribution deals will add thousands more retail locations in 2026, showing an independent restaurant brand scaling nationally through clean-label frozen pizza and adjacent pantry items.

competitors.name: Flour + Water Foods
competitors.action: Flour + Water entered frozen retail last month with Margherita, Pepperoni, and Cacio e Pepe pizzas in 12 Bay Area Whole Foods plus specialty grocers, using slow-fermented dough, par-bake plus flash-freeze, and chef-led positioning to bring a premium restaurant pizza into grocery.

trends.topic: Independent restaurant brands are entering frozen pizza with clean-label, craft-process positioning
trends.magnitude: Katie’s is adding thousands of new retail doors in 2026 while Flour + Water just launched into Whole Foods and specialty grocery
trends.context: The sharper competitive signal is no longer only big CPG incumbents. Credible restaurant operators are using naturally leavened dough, chef-led production, and selective grocery distribution to make frozen pizza feel closer to a restaurant experience.

breaking.headline: Restaurant-to-retail frozen pizza is accelerating on both ends of the market
breaking.impact: CPK is widening its global frozen footprint through Nestlé while independents like Katie’s and Flour + Water are proving that craft, clean-label pizza can scale into grocery. Real Dough is competing in a lane that is getting more crowded, but also more validated.
